title: Detect Peak Transaction Activity
real_world_story: A banking monitoring system records the number of transactions processed during consecutive time intervals. The system wants to identify the busiest continuous period of a fixed duration.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Transaction counts recorded during consecutive time intervals
real_world_connection.target_represents: Maximum transaction count within any continuous monitoring window
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A sliding window that efficiently moves across the transaction stream

problem_statement: Given an array of transaction counts recorded during N consecutive time intervals and an integer K, find the maximum total number of transactions processed in any continuous window of K intervals.
task: Find the maximum sum of transaction counts across any K consecutive intervals.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and K. The second line contains N space-separated integers representing transaction counts.
output_format: Print the maximum total number of transactions recorded in any K consecutive intervals.

examples.explanation: The window containing 15, 30, and 25 has the maximum total of 70 transactions.
The consecutive intervals containing 20 and 15 have the maximum total of 35 transactions.

expected_algorithm.name: Sliding Window
expected_algorithm.reason: A sliding window updates the sum when the window moves, avoiding recalculation of every K-element range.

hint: Calculate the sum of the first K transaction counts.
Move the window one position at a time.
Subtract the value leaving the window and add the new value.
Keep track of the maximum window sum.
real_world_takeaway: Sliding Window techniques allow monitoring systems to efficiently detect periods of unusually high transaction activity.
